claim: A confirmed-created bootstrap whose pane disappears before downstream completion permanently blocks archival of its selected existing thread because the design supplies no terminal abandonment path.
location: artifact.md:67,73,75,81,89; root spec Topology state machine and response loss, Human recovery, and Archival; canonical bootstrap task ht-qhz.2.3
evidence: Begin protects the existing thread, and the live fence never expires even when its seat retires (line 67). Missing pane or changed incarnation must refuse (line 73); completion is allowed only after canonical downstream completion and retained report validation (line 75). The only recovery decisions are created-pane adoption for an uncertain attempt and not-created assertion of inspected noncreation (line 81). Neither truthfully terminates a confirmed creation whose tab was subsequently closed, and no cancellation/abandonment command or state is specified anywhere in the bundled task tree. Consequently, a crash after recording creation followed by ordinary user tab closure leaves no legal path to complete the bootstrap or remove its thread archival veto (line 89). This concerns releasing durable workflow protection, not automatically closing topology.

claim: The recovery grammar lacks an expected-attempt binding, leaving stale recovery instructions able to apply an operator assertion to a later attempt than the one the operator inspected.
location: artifact.md:53,79,81,85; root spec CLI and compatibility and Human recovery; recovery task ht-qhz.6
evidence: The documented commands are human handoff recover REF --created-pane EXACT_PANE or --not-created (line 53), while recovery is required to reference an exact attempt (line 79), and not-created enables a distinct next attempt (line 81). The spec never defines REF as an immutable attempt-qualified recovery reference or exposes an expected-attempt parameter. A ready command retained while attempt A is uncertain can therefore be executed after another operator closes A and retry creates uncertain attempt B: resolving the same bootstrap REF to its current attempt applies an assertion based on inspection of A to B. Per-attempt deterministic keys and canonical contradictory-decision checks do not reject that newly selected B decision. The contract needs an immutable inspected-attempt reference in generated/user-facing recovery commands and stale-attempt refusal; the full recovery task specifies exact attempt references internally but no such user-to-attempt binding.

claim: The recovery CLI does not define a way to pin the operator assertion to the inspected creation attempt, allowing a delayed or repeated recovery invocation to be interpreted against a newer uncertain attempt.
location: artifact.md:53, 79–81 (recovery CLI and exact-attempt recovery/replay contract)
evidence: The only recovery grammar is `human handoff recover REF --created-pane EXACT_PANE` or `--not-created`; no expected-attempt argument or attempt-qualified REF semantics are defined. The canonical contract nevertheless says recovery references the "exact attempt", that not-created enables "a distinct next attempt", and that "Replaying either recovery key is presentation only". If an operator inspects attempt A, another recovery closes A, and a retry makes attempt B uncertain before the delayed command executes, resolving the bootstrap REF to the current attempt applies the old inspection assertion to B. Deterministic per-attempt mutation keys do not prevent this because choosing B produces a different key. The interface must define how the user-visible recovery invocation freezes A before the deciding transaction; neither the nested specs nor recovery task ht-qhz.6 supplies that binding.

claim: A bootstrap whose confirmed created pane disappears before downstream completion has no defined terminal abandonment path and therefore can protect its selected thread from archival indefinitely.
location: artifact.md:67, 73, 75, 81, 89 (live fence, missing-pane refusal, completion, recovery and archival)
evidence: Begin protects the existing selected thread, and the live fence "never expires or completes because a local file disappeared, a seat retired". A "missing pane" or "incarnation change" must refuse, while bootstrap completion is permitted "only after canonical downstream completion". Human recovery addresses an uncertain attempt: --created-pane asserts that an exact extant result belongs to it, and --not-created asserts inspected noncreation. For a durably confirmed creation that the user later closes before downstream handoff, neither assertion is truthful and the exact-topology rule prevents replacing the pane. The bundle defines no cancel/abandon transition, administrative archival release, or accepted permanent-protection limit for this state; its canonical command inventory and full task tree cover only reservation, evidence/recovery, attachment and successful completion. Consequently abandoning the unusable handoff cannot release its canonical archival protection even after the local journal is removed.

claim: The single mandatory seam task couples independently implementable native transport and canonical schema work to the external actor-routing integration, so unavailable peer actor source can stall work that does not consume it.
location: artifact.md: Follow-on and implementation ownership; tree-settled.json tasks ht-qhz.1, ht-qhz.3 and ht-qhz.2.1
evidence: The root requires that “only actual blocking shared boundaries gate their integration leaf, no global HOLD.” Yet ht-qhz.1 must land compilable protocol/CLI/journal dispatch wiring, consumes the “peer actor-route/classify_original_actor seam,” and requires original actor classification before new journal retry. Both ht-qhz.3 (typed native socket creation) and ht-qhz.2.1 (schema and canonical identity persistence) depend on completion of that entire task even though their consumed boundary is the topology data contract, not actor-route integration. The artifact provides no independently completable contract-only prerequisite or deferred actor-wiring subtask. Splitting the pure topology type boundary from actor-dependent dispatch would retain the declared interfaces without making that external integration a gate for these unrelated deliverables.

claim: A confirmed bootstrap whose exact pane disappears before downstream completion has no specified terminal abandonment path, so its existing-thread archival protection can remain permanently live.
location: artifact.md:67,73,75,81 (Topology state machine and response loss; Human recovery, authority and cleanup)
evidence: The spec says the live fence never expires or completes because a local file disappears or a seat retires (line 67), missing pane or incarnation change must refuse without relocating (line 73), and bootstrap completion requires canonical downstream completion (line 75). Its two recovery decisions concern uncertain creation: created-pane supplies creation evidence and not-created asserts noncreation (line 81). After confirmed creation, an independently closed pane or replaced host makes the required downstream path unavailable; asserting not-created would be false, and substituting another pane would violate the exact-topology contract. No cancellation/abandonment transition or operator procedure retires this fence while retaining honest creation inventory. The combined task tree adds no such transition.

claim: The recovery surface does not specify how a lost-reply operator invocation stays bound to its original attempt after agent retry advances the bootstrap to a later attempt.
evidence: The documented command is human handoff recover REF --not-created or --created-pane EXACT_PANE (line 53), with no attempt or recovery-operation selector. Mutation keys are children of compound and phase/attempt (line 63); recovery references an exact attempt and replaying its key must be presentation only, while not-created enables a distinct next attempt (line 81). Consider a committed not-created decision whose reply is lost, then an original-agent retry that reaches possible_creation on the next attempt, then a retry of the operator command. The design does not define a durable recovery invocation journal/key, expected-attempt precondition exposed to the operator, or other binding that prevents resolving REF to the newer attempt and treating the old inspection assertion as a new decision. Merely making each selected attempt/key idempotent does not resolve this cross-attempt ambiguity.

claim: The design leaves recovery from downstream-complete/bootstrap-incomplete crashes unspecified when the original live seat or host evidence becomes invalid before retry.
location: artifact.md:73,75 and bootstrap-coordinator section Downstream launch and terminal bootstrap replay (lines 177–183)
evidence: The downstream handoff has its own canonical completion, and only afterward can the bootstrap complete with validated retained presentation (line 75). These are separate named Complete commands and no atomic cross-completion transaction is specified. Retry ordinarily revalidates exact topology, incarnation and guarded seat mapping and refuses missing panes or changed incarnation (line 73); the explicit bypass and zero-effect retained presentation guarantee applies to a completed bootstrap (line 75 and line 183). A crash after downstream completion but before CompleteBootstrap therefore leaves an outer live fence even though all work is already terminal. If the host restarts or recipient binding changes before retry, the text does not require checking the attached downstream terminal state before those live guards, nor authorize finishing only the outer canonical bookkeeping from that retained result. The downstream-complete/outer-live intermediate state needs an explicit recovery branch and failure test; tests for an already completed bootstrap do not cover it.

claim: The recovery CLI does not specify how a saved recovery command binds to the inspected attempt, so replaying that command after a subsequent uncertain attempt cannot reliably distinguish presentation of the old decision from authorization to recover the new attempt.
location: artifact.md:53, 63, 79–85 (CLI and compatibility; Human recovery, authority and cleanup); ht-qhz.6 description
evidence: The advertised surface is `human handoff recover REF --created-pane EXACT_PANE` or `--not-created`, while ordinary `retry REF` advances the same bootstrap through distinct attempts. The contract requires recovery to reference the "exact attempt", makes mutation keys children of the compound and phase/attempt, and says "Replaying either recovery key is presentation only". Neither the grammar nor the task tree defines an attempt-qualified REF, an explicit expected-attempt argument, or a separately published durable recovery reference. Consider successful --not-created for attempt A, retry creating uncertain attempt B, then re-execution of the previously emitted --not-created command for A: selecting the current attempt B applies an inspection assertion to the wrong attempt, while always selecting A makes the displayed syntax insufficient to recover B. The exact attempt must be frozen in an operator-visible invocation/reference, not inferred from the mutable current attempt.

claim: A confirmed creation whose pane disappears before downstream completion permanently blocks archival of its selected existing thread under the specified transitions, because the design provides no terminal abandonment or repair path for that bootstrap.
location: artifact.md:67, 73–75, 81, 89 (Topology state machine and response loss; Human recovery; Archival and compatibility); canonical-bootstrap nested spec
evidence: Begin protects the selected existing thread; the live fence never expires because local state disappears or a seat retires. Retry must refuse "missing pane, incarnation change" without relocating, and bootstrap completion requires canonical downstream completion. The recovery options address an uncertain creation: --created-pane records the asserted result of that attempt and --not-created asserts noncreation. Neither is truthful when creation was durably confirmed but a human later closed the exact pane before launch. The listed canonical commands and complete task tree provide no abandon/cancel transition that retains the evidence while releasing archival protection. Thus an ordinary post-creation topology loss leaves a permanent live veto even though all safe automatic effects correctly refuse; an explicit administrative terminal disposition or an explicitly accepted permanent-veto limit is missing.

claim: The bootstrap has no terminal abandonment transition, so a confirmed creation that becomes permanently unusable before downstream completion leaves its selected thread permanently protected from archival.
location: artifact.md lines 67, 73–75, 81, 89: Topology state machine and response loss; Human recovery; Archival and compatibility
evidence: Begin protects an existing selected thread; the live fence never completes because a seat retired or a local file disappeared (line 67). A missing created pane or changed host incarnation must refuse retry (line 73), and bootstrap completion requires canonical downstream completion (line 75). Consider confirmed creation recorded before attachment, followed by deletion of that pane: retry cannot proceed and cannot recreate. The two recovery operations address uncertain creation only: --created-pane cannot truthfully adopt a replacement, and --not-created cannot truthfully assert that no creation happened (line 81). The fence continues vetoing archival (line 89). No cancel/abandon transition, operator release of protection, or explicit acceptance of this permanent archival blockage appears in the root, nested specs, or task descriptions. The same missing lifecycle exit matters if the frozen original actor permanently loses authority before downstream work.

claim: The recovery CLI does not specify how a repeated recovery invocation remains pinned to the attempt the operator inspected after a lost response and advancement to a later attempt.
location: artifact.md lines 53, 63, 81, 85: recovery grammar and exact-attempt recovery contract; task ht-qhz.6
evidence: The only public recovery grammar is human handoff recover REF --created-pane EXACT_PANE or --not-created (line 53). Decisions must reference an exact attempt, keys are children of phase/attempt, and replaying a recovery key must be presentation-only (lines 63 and 81), but the contract never defines REF as an attempt-specific recovery reference, exposes an expected-attempt/key argument, or persists a recovery invocation identity before submission. If --not-created for attempt A commits but its reply is lost, an original-agent retry can reserve attempt B before the operator repeats the same displayed recovery command. Resolving the compound REF to the latest attempt then constructs a new B recovery key, so key-level idempotency does not preserve the operator's original assertion about A. The design needs to specify the mechanism tying the inspection and recovery command to A across response loss; listing attempt IDs in reports (line 85) and retaining exact decisions alone does not define that mechanism.

claim: The retry contract does not define how to finish a still-live bootstrap after its downstream handoff has canonically completed and current caller or topology guards subsequently fail.
location: artifact.md, root spec “Topology state machine and response loss”, paragraphs beginning “The result records” and “After attachment”; nested bootstrap coordinator “Downstream launch and terminal bootstrap replay”; ht-qhz.4.3 and ht-qhz.2.3.
evidence: The root requires “Current host reads and canonical ordinary guarded seat resolution must still confirm that exact topology, same incarnation and mapping” and refuses missing panes/incarnation changes. It separately says “The bootstrap is completed only after canonical downstream completion and retained terminal report validation”, with the guard-bypassing presentation path described only for “Completed bootstrap”. Therefore downstream Complete can commit, the coordinator can crash before CompleteBootstrap, and the pane or original caller binding can change before retry. The downstream is terminal but the bootstrap is still live. The combined contract specifies neither atomic completion of both fences nor an early downstream-terminal reconciliation path that can validate the retained result and complete the bootstrap without re-running live caller/topology/resolution guards. Existing completed-bootstrap tests do not specify this intermediate two-fence state. The missing transition can strand an already-finished handoff behind live bootstrap archival protection.

claim: A bootstrap whose confirmed created pane disappears before downstream completion has no specified terminal failure or abandonment path, leaving its selected thread protected indefinitely.
location: artifact.md, root spec “Topology state machine and response loss”, “Human recovery, authority and cleanup”, and “Archival and compatibility”; canonical bootstrap nested spec and ht-qhz.6.
evidence: Begin protects the selected existing thread, and the root says the live fence “never expires or completes because a local file disappeared, a seat retired” while retry must refuse a “missing pane” or “incarnation change”. Completion requires canonical downstream completion. The only operator transitions are --created-pane for an “uncertain attempt” and --not-created, which asserts actual noncreation and opens another attempt. After durable confirmed creation, followed by the pane being closed before downstream completion, neither assertion truthfully applies and exact retry cannot progress. The archival section explicitly makes a valid bootstrap selecting an existing thread a veto. No cancellation, abandoned/failed terminal state, or explicit operator retirement of that protection appears in the combined state machine or full task tree. This gap does not require automatically closing topology, adopting another pane, resetting a start gate, or weakening the existing noncreation assertion; it requires specifying how permanently unfinishable work can end while retaining its honest historical evidence.
